questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a lineage arrow between two datasets usually represent, beyond 'connects to'?
options: A transformation — logic such as a filter, join, calculation, or mapping applied to the data
A simple file copy with no changes
A physical network cable between two servers
A permissions boundary between two teams
questions.explain: Almost no hop in a real pipeline is a straight copy — something happens at each one, and that something is the transformation.

questions.q: What is a 'business rule' as described in this lesson?
options: Logic that encodes an organizational decision, embedded inside a transformation
A company's formal HR policy document
Any SQL statement regardless of what it does
A naming convention applied to table names
questions.explain: A business rule is the organizational decision behind the mechanics — e.g. which Discount field to use, or whether Revenue includes tax — tangled into the transformation's logic.

questions.q: In the Revenue = Price * Quantity - Discount example, what does the lesson identify as the actual business-rule question?
options: Which Discount field is being used, and whether Revenue includes tax
Whether multiplication is calculated correctly by the database engine
Whether Price is stored as an integer or a decimal
Whether the formula uses uppercase or lowercase field names
questions.explain: The arithmetic itself is mechanical; the real ambiguity is which specific Discount field is used and whether tax is included — decisions made once and often forgotten.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a transformation-logic change is more dangerous than a rename?
options: Because the column name, type, and location can stay identical while the business rule behind it silently changes
Because renames are always backward-incompatible
Because transformation changes are illegal under most data governance policies
Because logic changes always increase the size of the dataset
questions.explain: A rename is visible and easy to document. A logic change can happen with the structure completely unchanged, making it invisible to lineage documentation that only tracks structure.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect transformations back to the business glossary from the Metadata Management course?
options: A transformation is where a glossary term's definition either does or doesn't get honored in actual code, so checking that match is part of documenting lineage well
The business glossary replaces the need for any transformation logic
Glossary terms are automatically generated from transformation code with no review needed
Transformations and glossary terms are unrelated concepts
questions.explain: A mismatch between a transformation's actual logic and its glossary definition is a common, quiet source of numbers that don't reconcile between reports.
